newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-VENABLES UPBEAT ABOUT PROSPECTS OF AUSTRALIAN JOB.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VENABLES UPBEAT ABOUT PROSPECTS OF AUSTRALIAN JOB.

text.p: Australian soccer officials confirmed on Sunday they had held talks with Terry Venables but said the former England team boss had not yet been signed as Australia's new coach.

Soccer Australia (SA) spokesman Steve Speziale told reporters in Sydney that SA chairman David Hill had held discussions with a number of leading coaches on a visit to Europe over the past week, including Venables, former Ireland manager Jack Charlton, ex-Barcelona coach Johan Cruyff and former Leeds manager Howard Wilkinson.

"There's no denying that David has spoken with (Venables), but he's also spoken with Jack Charlton, Johan Cryuff and (he) told me today that he had dinner with Leeds' Howard Wilkinson last night," Speziale said.
Venables, quoted in Britain's News of the World on Sunday, said he was now "99 percent in position," with a bumper pay-day on the horizon.
A delighted Venables, who has only recently become director of football with first division strugglers Portsmouth, said: "I couldn't be more upbeat.
"The job offers me one thing I have always wanted -- to be involved in a World Cup. I wanted it with England, but it wasn't to be. In the circumstances the offer from Australia is exciting.
"There are a couple of details to be sorted out, but I don't see any major problem. I hope and believe everything will be finalised very quickly."

Hill left Australia last week for a FIFA meeting in Zurich, saying at the time he was happy to talk to anyone about the Australia position after long-time coach Eddie Thomson quit last month for Hiroshima in the Japanese J-League.
Speziale added that, while Venables was "very interested" in the Australian job, a deal was yet to be finalised.

Australian media reported last week that Venables could be appointed under a novel job-sharing scheme that would allow him to spend most of his time in Europe and monitor the form of Australian players there in the lead-up to the 1998 World Cup finals in France.
Australia has more than 100 overseas-based players, including Aston Villa goalkeeper Mark Bosnich and Lazio sweeper Paul Okon.
